dataset_provenance: SPRSound (SJTU Paediatric Respiratory Sound Database) CC BY 4.0

primary_target.name: SPRSound Pediatric Acoustic Record Classification (Adventitious Sound Types)
primary_target.description: Classification of pediatric auscultation recordings into baseline normal and adventitious respiratory sound categories, with poor-quality recordings handled via explicit exclusion.

class_descriptions.Normal: Clear vesicular breath sounds without adventitious noises.
class_descriptions.CAS: Continuous Adventitious Sounds (wheezes or rhonchi present in breath cycles).
class_descriptions.DAS: Discontinuous Adventitious Sounds (fine or coarse crackles present in breath cycles).
class_descriptions.CAS & DAS: Co-occurrence of both continuous (wheezes/rhonchi) and discontinuous (crackles) adventitious sounds.

quality_handling.rationale: Poor quality recordings exhibit heavy acoustic noise, crying, sensor movement, or uninterpretable SNR. Including them as a disease or sound class pollutes acoustic representations. In production inference, recordings with poor signal quality are rejected before adventitious classification.

quality_detection_target.name: SPRSound Acoustic Classification with Explicit Quality State
quality_detection_target.description: 5-class acoustic classification including signal quality triage.

ternary_target.name: SPRSound Challenge Task 2-1 (Ternary)
ternary_target.description: High-level tri-state classification: Normal, Adventitious (CAS, DAS, CAS&DAS), and Poor Quality.

event_level_target.name: SPRSound Challenge Task 1-2 (Event Level Multiclass)
event_level_target.description: Classification of segmented respiratory cycle intervals based on expert acoustic annotations.

clinical_disease_distinction.warning: Clinical disease labels in SPRSound are patient-level discharge/admission diagnoses (e.g., Pneumonia, Asthma, Bronchitis). They are NOT recording-level acoustic labels. Assigning a patient's pneumonia diagnosis to a recording at chest location p3 that contains purely normal breath sounds induces severe label noise and clinical inconsistency. True clinical disease diagnosis requires multi-site pooling and clinical evidence integration.
